How to install Claude Code on a Mac: native installer, Homebrew or npm

Reviewed: 2026-11-20 · WodeMac

Claude Code installs on macOS 13 or later in three official ways: the native installer (curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash, recommended and self-updating), Homebrew (brew install --cask claude-code) or npm (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest, Node.js 22+). It needs 4GB of RAM and an internet connection. To sign in you need a Claude Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan or a Claude Console account; the free plan does not include Claude Code. A WodeMac Mac mini arrives with Claude Code preinstalled, so you only sign in.

Requirements and accounts

According to the official setup docs, Claude Code runs on macOS 13.0 or later with 4GB+ RAM on an x64 or ARM64 processor, and it needs an internet connection. The agent itself is light because the model runs on Anthropic's servers; what uses your Mac's resources is your own project's builds and tests.

To sign in you need a Claude Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise subscription, or a Claude Console account with API credits. The free claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. Your account must be your own or your company's and follow Anthropic's supported-country rules; where the Mac is located does not change that. WodeMac does not provide, hold or share Claude accounts.

Three official install methods

The native installer is the recommended method and updates itself in the background:

curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

Homebrew has two casks: claude-code follows the stable channel, usually about a week behind, and claude-code@latest gets each release as it ships. Homebrew installs do not update themselves; run brew upgrade claude-code.

brew install --cask claude-code

npm needs Node.js 22 or later and installs the same native binary. Do not use sudo; run the same command again to upgrade:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest

Open a new terminal and run claude --version. If the shell cannot find claude, the install directory is not on your PATH yet. claude doctor prints install health, settings errors and update status without starting a session.

First sign-in and first task

  1. Open a terminal in your project directory and run claude.
  2. Sign in through the browser with your Claude account. If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and you approve it, Claude Code uses the key instead.
  3. Confirm that you trust the directory to start the session.
  4. Ask it to run the project's existing build or tests first, then give it one small, clearly scoped task.
  5. Review the diff before committing, and say which directories and secrets it must not touch.

Type /login inside a session to switch accounts, and claude update to update by hand.

On a WodeMac Mac mini

A WodeMac dedicated Mac mini comes with Claude Code and Codex installed and admin rights for you, so you can skip the install. Open the Mac through the preinstalled remote desktop app, open a terminal in your project and run claude, then sign in with your own account.

The Mac stays online 24/7 in California, which suits long tasks: keep sessions in tmux or continue them from your phone with Remote Control. The price covers the machine only; Claude usage is billed by Anthropic to your account.

FAQ

Can I use Claude Code with a free Claude account?

No. The official docs say Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise or Console account; the free claude.ai plan does not include it.

Which install method should I use on a Mac?

The native installer, unless you manage tools with Homebrew or npm. It is the recommended method and the only one that updates itself in the background.

How do I check that Claude Code installed correctly?

Open a new terminal and run claude --version. For a fuller check of install health and settings, run claude doctor.

Do I need to install Claude Code on a WodeMac Mac mini?

No. It is preinstalled at delivery; sign in with your own account and run claude update when you want the latest version.
